subject: Sparrow Labs — SDK concordance & tracing hooks proposal
messages:
From: Alex Chen <alex.chen@sparrowlabs.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Priya Rao <priya.rao@sparrowlabs.com>
Date: Mon, 02 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Sparrow x Redwood — SDK concordance and tracing hooks

Hi Neha,

Thanks again for the intro. Sparrow Labs is exploring a closer product integration with Redwood so customers that embed our retrieval/augmentation SDK can get first-class tracing and attribution through Redwood’s runtime. We put together a short spec outlining a) a lightweight adapter for our client SDK, b) a tracing hook that surfaces per-request model selection and token counts, and c) an auth flow to preserve tenant isolation.

Attached: sparrow_sdk_spec_v1.pdf (high-level API and example instrumentation).

High-level asks from our side:
- A quick feasibility read from Redwood’s runtime team (are the tracing events we propose reasonable?)
- A recommended place in your SDK catalog to publish a joint adapter (hosted vs dedicated config guidance)
- Proposed mutual action plan and timeline for a co-marketing pilot

Can we sync this week for 30 minutes? Priya (cc’d) will be our technical lead on the integration. She can do Wed/Thu afternoon PT.

Appreciate it — excited about the potential.

Best,
Alex Chen
Head of Platform Partnerships
Sparrow Labs

--

Alex / Priya —

Thanks for the spec, Alex. I reviewed the PDF at a high level and it looks sensible. Looping in Vanessa (Partner Tech Lead) and Marissa (SDK Program Manager) so they can triage technical feasibility and surface any compatibility constraints.

Initial responses:
- Tracing events: the runtime can emit hook points for model selection, latency, and token counts. We need to validate the exact event schema in the spec; that’s a quick follow-up.
- Adapter placement: we typically publish partner adapters in the ISV catalog with clear host/dedicated labels; Marissa will propose the onboarding checklist.
- Tenant isolation / auth: we prefer an opaque token exchange (short-lived delegation token) for cross-service calls — Vanessa, can you confirm the recommended flow?

I can do Wed 11/04 2:30–3:00pm PT for a sync. Priya — does that work? If yes, Vanessa will send a calendar invite and a short mutual action plan template for review.

Regards,
Neha Kapoor
Director, Partnerships & Alliances
Redwood Inference

Hi Neha / Vanessa —

Thanks for the quick reply. Wed 11/04 2:30pm PT works for me — I’ll join. A few clarifying notes so the 30-minute sync can be focused:

1) Tracing schema: we’re proposing three event types — request.start, model.resolve, request.complete — with JSON payloads including request_id, user_tenant_id, model_id, latency_ms, tokens_in, tokens_out. Open to adjustments but we want to avoid per-token events for verbosity reasons.

2) Auth / tenant isolation: proposed flow is what Neha called “delegation token” — Sparrow issues an ephemeral signed token per tenant that Redwood validates and maps to a partner-scoped principal. We can demo a sample exchange during the call.

3) Backcompat: Sparrow’s current SDKs support callback-style instrumentation. We can add a Redwood-specific adapter shim that calls into your runtime hook. We’d like guidance on versioning and minimum supported SDK versions.

Attached: mutual_action_plan.xlsx (draft timeline + owners).

Looking forward to the call.

—Priya
Engineering Manager, Integrations
Sparrow Labs

Alex / Priya — great sync today, thanks for walking through the spec. Below is a concise next-step plan from Redwood with owners and timelines so we have one place to track progress. I’ll also upload this to the HubSpot deal record.

Redwood proposed action items (shortened):
1) Event schema confirmation (due 11/10) — Owner: Marissa Cole (we’ll provide a JSON schema and minimal example)
2) Auth flow PoC (due 11/17) — Owner: Vanessa Ortiz (engineering liaison) + Sparrow engs to exchange a demo token flow
3) Adapter prototype (due 11/30) — Owner: Sparrow (Priya) with Redwood SDK review & acceptance criterion from Marissa
4) Co-marketing pilot plan (content + joint blog/demo) — Draft due 12/08 — Owner: Neha Kapoor + Sparrow Partnerships

Compatibility notes from engineering:
- Runtime: the tracing points you propose are acceptable; we’ll expect a compact payload (request_id, model_id, tenant_id, tokens_in, tokens_out, duration_ms). Avoid large nested payloads.
- Backfill: if a customer runs a mixed fleet (hosted + dedicated), Redwood will surface the events from the active runtime in the console; adapter needs no special work for that beyond tagging events with runtime_id.

Attachments: mutual_action_plan.xlsx (redwood-reviewed draft) — please confirm owners in the spreadsheet.

Next meeting: 11/17 10:00am PT for the auth PoC lab — calendar invite sent.

Thanks — let’s keep this lean and iterate the adapter in a short sprint.

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Partner Tech Lead
Redwood Inference
